paragraphs.source_en: After the war ended, Tokugawa Ieyasu ordered that all postwar affairs be settled within a hundred days, but everything was concluded ten days earlier than he had expected.

paragraphs.source_en: On the morning of the fourth day of the eighth month in the first year of Genna (1615), Ieyasu departed from Kyoto.

paragraphs.source_en: Matsudaira Kazusa-no-suke Tadateru followed close behind his father in leaving Kyoto. Matsudaira Ōsumi-no-kami Shigekatsu, father of Matsudaira Katsutaka, was responsible for directing the Echigo army's withdrawal.

units.source_en: Matsudaira Kazusa-no-suke Tadateru followed close behind his father in leaving Kyoto.

paragraphs.source_en: After Ōkubo Nagayasu died and Minagawa Yamashiro-no-kami was also dismissed, Ōsumi-no-kami Shigekatsu became one of Tadateru's senior retainers and took up residence at Sanjō Castle in Echigo.

units.source_en: After Ōkubo Nagayasu died and Minagawa Yamashiro-no-kami was also dismissed, Ōsumi-no-kami Shigekatsu became one of Tadateru's senior retainers and took up residence at Sanjō Castle in Echigo.
units.source_zh: 大久保长安死后，皆川山城守也被撤职，之后大隅守重胜便作为忠辉家老，居于越后的三条城。

paragraphs.source_zh: 大久保长安死后，皆川山城守也被撤职，之后大隅守重胜便作为忠辉家老，居于越后的三条城。

paragraphs.source_en: Sanjō lay north of Takada, a considerable distance from Takada Castle, between the domains of Date and Tadateru, keeping the two apart. Ōsumi-no-kami Shigekatsu appeared to have chosen the place precisely so that he could keep a covert watch, but Tadateru paid it no heed.

units.source_en: Sanjō lay north of Takada, a considerable distance from Takada Castle, between the domains of Date and Tadateru, keeping the two apart.

paragraphs.source_en: Some might have taken offense at this, supposing that Date was waiting for the Ōgosho to die, but Tadateru felt no resentment; he believed his father-in-law had not yet abandoned the idea of making him lord of Osaka Castle.

paragraphs.source_en: On the tenth day of the eighth month, Ieyasu entered Nagoya with Yoshinao and Yorinobu.

units.source_en: On the tenth day of the eighth month, Ieyasu entered Nagoya with Yoshinao and Yorinobu.

paragraphs.source_en: He will probably rest here for two or three days. So much the better, Tadateru thought. But when he saw the gleaming golden shachi atop Nagoya Castle, his heart jolted: My brothers possess such magnificent castles, while mine is nowhere near the equal of this. He felt both envy and a measure of bitterness.

paragraphs.source_en: Things did not go as Tadateru wished; in the end, Osaka Castle was temporarily placed under Matsudaira Tadaaki's charge. Tadaaki was the fourth son of Okudaira Mimasaka-no-kami Nobumasa, and his mother was Kamehime, the eldest daughter born to Ieyasu and Lady Tsukiyama. Though Osaka Castle would eventually come under the shogunate's direct control, Ieyasu rejected his son's request and entrusted it to his daughter's son instead. However one considered it, the decision was difficult to understand.

units.source_en: Things did not go as Tadateru wished; in the end, Osaka Castle was temporarily placed under Matsudaira Tadaaki's charge.

paragraphs.source_zh: 事情未能如忠辉所愿，大坂城最终由松平忠明暂管。忠明乃是奥平美作守信昌四男，其母乃家康和筑山夫人所生长女龟姬。虽说大坂城终究会为幕府直辖，但家康却拒绝了儿子之求，将它交与外孙管理。里外一思，总让人有些想不通。

paragraphs.source_en: If it were mine, I would invite great merchant ships from overseas, build a major harbor here, and trade openly with foreign lands. But if I simply withdraw to Takada Castle, I fear Osaka Castle will remain beyond my reach for the rest of my life. The golden shachi atop Nagoya Castle had wounded Tadateru's pride. He wondered: When Father is in good spirits, might Mother be able to help me attain my wish?

units.source_en: If it were mine, I would invite great merchant ships from overseas, build a major harbor here, and trade openly with foreign lands. But if I simply withdraw to Takada Castle, I fear Osaka Castle will remain beyond my reach for the rest of my life.

paragraphs.source_en: The next day, his mother, Lady Chaa, came to Tadateru's residence. Tadateru could have gone into the castle to visit his mother, but custom made that inconvenient in many ways. Matsudaira Kazusa-no-suke Tadateru was the Ōgosho's son. Though Lady Chaa had borne him as a concubine, her station still made her Tadateru's servant. Thus, although Lady Chaa had come to see her own son, the visit had to be described as paying her respects to her lord.
